question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Starch: Egg yolk**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Starch is a carbohydrate consisting of a large number of glucose units joined by glycosidic bonds.
 
• It is produced by most green plants as an energy store.
 
• Egg yolk does not contain starch; it is rich in proteins and fats.
 
• Common sources of starch include potatoes, rice, wheat, and corn.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lactose**

 
 
• Lactose is a disaccharide sugar derived from galactose and glucose that is found in milk.
 
• It makes up around 2-8% of milk (by weight).
 
• Lactose is important for the proper digestion of milk in mammals.
 
 
 
• **Fructose**
 
 
• Fructose is a simple sugar found in many plants, where it is often bonded to glucose to form the disaccharide sucrose.
 
• It is one of the three dietary monosaccharides, along with glucose and galactose, that are absorbed directly into the bloodstream during digestion.
 
• Fructose is commonly found in fruits such as grapes, apples, and honey.
 
 
 
• **Maltose**
 
 
• Maltose, also known as malt sugar, is a disaccharide formed from two units of glucose joined with an α(1→4) bond.
 
• It is found in germinating grains like wheat, cornmeal, and barley.
 
• Maltose is used in the brewing of beer and is a component of malt.
